subject.title: Skills silently truncated - user-created skills invisible with no warning or prioritization

question: Should OpenClaw address this issue first with the narrow omitted-key visibility fix, a new priority/pinning config surface, broader smart/lazy skill indexing, or a staged combination?
rationale: The source-level truncation gap is real, but priority/pinning and context-aware loading would change core prompt policy and public config shape, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive maintainer product direction.

options.title: Stage narrow visibility first
options.body: Land or repair the omitted-key recovery path in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/42637, then evaluate priority and smart loading separately.

options.title: Design priority/pinning first
options.body: Hold the narrow fix until maintainers choose a durable `skills.entries` or per-context required-skills config contract.

options.title: Move to smart indexing
options.body: Treat this issue as part of a broader lazy-loading or skill-search architecture tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89361.

recommendation.title: Stage narrow visibility first
recommendation.body: Land or repair the omitted-key recovery path in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/42637, then evaluate priority and smart loading separately.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent skills prompt history and direct engagement on the open omitted-key PR that is the best first repair path.
